newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares up 100 points after Friday's slide.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares up 100 points after Friday's slide.

text.p: Swiss shares bounced back from Friday's fall of nearly two percent in a technical reaction that pushed stocks up more than 100 points to close at the day's highs on Monday, dealers said.
Short-covering, firming Swiss bonds and a rising U.S. dollar were seen as other major reasons for the advance.
"In spite of Friday's correction, the general upward trend should last a while," one dealer said, adding there was enough liquidity to continue to bolster prices.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 108.4 points, or 2.15 percent, to 5,150.0. The broad Swiss Performance Index gained 63.27 points to 3,258.83.
Bourse volume stood at 2.35 billion francs.
Developments depended now on Wall Street and the situation in France and Germany, dealers said.

One trader said uncertainty about Europe's economic and monetary union was rising given the Socialist victory in French parliamentary elections and controversy over the revaluation of German gold reserves.

Zurich Group was one of the biggest winners among blue-chips, adding 18 francs, or more than three percent, to 538 francs. Dealers said continued speculation the insurer was close to acquiring U.S. money manament firm Scudder gave the stock a boost.
Zurich said it had successfully placed $1 billion in 40-year capital securities but added the placement was not linked to a specific transaction.

Among financials, CS Group and SBC also posted gains. UBS bearers, which led the actives list, climbed 39 francs to 1,591. UBS chairman Robert Studer said he expected "very good" 1997 first half results.
Industrials ABB, Holderbank and SMH were up more than three percent each.
